The Guardian (Conservatives) — datePublished 2026-10-25T13:00:03Z = 13:00 GMT Sun 25 Oct; dateModified 2026-10-25T17:15:35Z = 17:15 GMT. Both after the cutover, so Z = local. Retrieved by curl at 17:32 GMT.

HEADLINE: "Former Tory candidate suspended over contract killer claims was adviser in Kemi Badenoch's office"
STANDFIRST: "Sources close to Tory leader say Jack Ross, who faces party investigation after undercover report, worked as social media consultant"
BYLINE: Ben Quinn and Jessica Elgot

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED, AND BY WHOM
"A former Conservative election candidate who was suspended after he was filmed discussing the cost of hiring contract killers worked as a consultant in Kemi Badenoch's office as recently as last year."
"It has now emerged that he was working in 2025 in the leader of the opposition's office, which can draw on taxpayer funds to pay staff."
The role itself is sourced to the leader's own side: "Sources close to Badenoch said Ross was contracted as a junior social media external consultant in her office." So the proximity to the leader's office is confirmed by Badenoch's own camp, not merely alleged — but the characterisation of the role as junior and external is theirs.
A corroborating but anonymous account: "a Tory staffer familiar with the role of Ross at that time said: 'Jack would come and go in the office and a few people raised their eyebrows, but it was brushed under the carpet because he got the party clicks on socials. He would have been in the same room as Kemi and she would have been aware of him. Some MPs were uncomfortable about it, but senior figures were clear that social media clicks were more important.'" This is an unnamed staffer.
Ross's other roles, uncontested: former Conservative local election candidate (stood unsuccessfully); CEO of Turning Point UK since 2021. Footage released by TPUK last year showed Ross and others from the group meeting Badenoch after Charlie Kirk's death.

WHAT THE PARTY SAYS NOW
A Tory spokesperson: "Mr Ross's membership of the Conservative party has been suspended with immediate effect pending an investigation. We cannot comment further while the investigation is ongoing."

CHARGES — THERE ARE NONE
"Police in Scotland say they will be reviewing an Al Jazeera documentary in which Ross was filmed making a range comments about what a contract killer could be employed to do." A review of a broadcast is not an investigation into an offence and is not a charge. No one has been charged. Ross and Nick Tenconi have been approached for comment by the Guardian and have not responded to it.

A DIRECT CONFLICT WITH THE BBC ON THE EMPLOYMENT FACT
The BBC, https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c63r5779vyl9o, datePublished 2026-10-24T02:52:10Z = 03:52 BST Sat 24 Oct (before the cutover), says: "Jack Ross was contracted to do social media work for the party until earlier this year, the BBC has been told... Ross was paid to provide social media advice to the party for a brief period, the BBC has been told. He was never an employee or Conservative Campaign Headquarters pass holder." The BBC places the work at the PARTY / CCHQ and dates it to "until earlier this year", i.e. into 2026.
The Guardian places the work in the LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION'S OFFICE, taxpayer-funded, and dates it to 2025.
These are different employers and different dates. Both are sourced to unnamed insiders. Do not merge them into one sentence.
The BBC also contradicts itself internally: its image caption says "Jack Ross (pictured) held the post of Chief Operations Officer at Turning Point UK", while its body text calls him "chief executive of Turning Point UK". The Guardian has Ross as CEO and Nick Tenconi, the Ukip leader, as COO. The BBC caption appears to be wrong.
The BBC adds Badenoch's own words on the allegations: she called them "shocking allegations", adding that she did not "believe that person is a member anymore".
Both outlets report Ross's denial: per the BBC, "Al Jazeera said Ross denied the finding 'completely' and claimed everything he said to the reporter was not meant seriously."

THE UNDERLYING ALLEGATION — RECORDED HERE FOR COMPLETENESS, NOT RECOMMENDED FOR PUBLICATION
Al Jazeera (approved source, newsroom) broadcast undercover filming this week in which Ross appears to offer to "broker" the services of contract killers, after an undercover reporter approached him in 2022 with a fictitious family-business scenario. The filmed remarks are quoted at length by the Guardian and include an itemised list of violent acts. The allegation is uncharged, denied, and rests on undercover filming of a private conversation four years ago. The reportable new fact today is the proximity to the leader's office and the taxpayer funding, not the killing claim.
